from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Tangent lines approximate curves at a point.",
            "They predict where the curve crosses the axis.",
            "This allows us to estimate roots numerically."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisites: The Geometry of a Tangent", lecture_lines)
        
        # Create function and axes
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-1, 5], y_range=[-1, 4], axis_config={"include_tip": False})
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.2*(x-1)*(x-3)*(x-4) + 2, color=WHITE)
        
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B1", "E6", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.add(axes, curve)
        
        # Elements for animation
        x0_val = 1.2
        # Fixed: Removed non-existent p2y() method; directly using coordinates
        x0_point = Dot(axes.c2p(x0_val, 0.2*(x0_val-1)*(x0_val-3)*(x0_val-4) + 2), color=YELLOW)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(Create(x0_point))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(ORANGE))
        
        # Tangent line (simplified approximation)
        # Point (x0, f(x0))
        f_x0 = 0.2*(x0_val-1)*(x0_val-3)*(x0_val-4) + 2
        # Slope (derivative approx)
        df_x0 = 0.6*x0_val**2 - 4*x0_val + 6.2
        
        tangent = Line(
            axes.c2p(x0_val-1, f_x0 - df_x0),
            axes.c2p(x0_val+1, f_x0 + df_x0),
            color=PURPLE
        )
        self.play(Create(tangent))
        
        # Intersection x1
        x1_val = x0_val - f_x0 / df_x0
        x1_point = Dot(axes.c2p(x1_val, 0), color=RED)
        self.play(Create(x1_point))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(RED))
        
        label_x0 = MathTex("x_0").next_to(x0_point, UP, buff=0.1)
        label_x1 = MathTex("x_1").next_to(x1_point, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        self.play(Write(label_x0), Write(label_x1))
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Newton’s Method: The Iterative Search", [
            "Newton's formula iteratively improves our guess.",
            "We calculate the next point using the derivative.",
            "Repeating this refines the root estimate rapidly."
        ])
        
        # Define the function and axis
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-1, 5], y_range=[-1, 5], axis_config={"include_tip": False})
        self.place_in_area(axes, "B1", "E6", scale_factor=0.6)
        
        func = lambda x: (x - 2)**2 + 0.5
        graph = axes.plot(func, color=BLUE)
        self.add(axes, graph)
        
        x0 = 4.0
        dot_x0 = Dot(axes.c2p(x0, func(x0)), color=YELLOW)
        label_x0 = MathTex("x_0").next_to(dot_x0, UP)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(dot_x0, label_x0))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Tangent line at x0
        slope = 2 * (x0 - 2)
        tangent = Line(
            axes.c2p(x0 - 1, func(x0) - slope), 
            axes.c2p(x0 + 1, func(x0) + slope), 
            color=RED
        )
        self.play(Create(tangent))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(RED)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Jump to x1
        x1 = x0 - func(x0) / slope
        dot_x1 = Dot(axes.c2p(x1, 0), color=GREEN)
        label_x1 = MathTex("x_1").next_to(dot_x1, DOWN)
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(tangent),
            FadeIn(dot_x1, label_x1)
        )
        self.lecture[2].set_color(GREEN)
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Your starting guess decides which root you find.",
            "The number line divides into basins of attraction.",
            "Points near boundaries jump between different roots."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Basin of Attraction", lecture_lines)
        
        # Create visual elements
        # A simple number line representation of basins
        line = NumberLine(x_range=[-3, 3], length=5).shift(DOWN * 1.5)
        
        # Basins of attraction simulation (using colored regions)
        # Root at -1 (left), Root at 1 (right)
        basin1 = Rectangle(width=2.5, height=2, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.3).shift(LEFT * 1.25)
        basin2 = Rectangle(width=2.5, height=2, color=RED, fill_opacity=0.3).shift(RIGHT * 1.25)
        
        # Point to be moved
        dot = Dot(color=YELLOW).move_to(line.n2p(0))
        
        self.place_in_area(VGroup(line, basin1, basin2, dot), "B2", "E5")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(Indicate(dot))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        self.play(Create(basin1), Create(basin2))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(ORANGE))
        self.play(dot.animate.move_to(line.n2p(-1.5)), run_time=1.5)
        self.play(dot.animate.move_to(line.n2p(1.5)), run_time=1.5)
        self.play(dot.animate.move_to(line.n2p(0)), run_time=1)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("From Roots to Fractals: Newton's Fractal", [
            "Extend this process to the complex plane.",
            "Initial guesses now lead to different complex roots.",
            "Fractal patterns emerge along the basin boundaries.",
            "Even small shifts cause wildly different outcomes.",
            "This illustrates extreme sensitivity to initial conditions."
        ])
        
        # Elements
        complex_plane = ComplexPlane(x_range=[-2, 2, 1], y_range=[-2, 2, 1], axis_config={"include_numbers": False}).scale(0.5)
        basin = Square(side_length=2, fill_opacity=0.6, color=BLUE).set_fill(BLUE, opacity=0.3)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.place_at_grid(complex_plane, 'C3', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Create(complex_plane))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        self.place_in_area(basin, 'B2', 'D4', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(FadeIn(basin))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        # Simple representation of patterns
        pattern = VGroup(*[Dot(point=np.array([np.random.uniform(-0.8, 0.8), np.random.uniform(-0.8, 0.8), 0]), radius=0.03, color=TEAL) for _ in range(50)])
        self.place_in_area(pattern, 'B2', 'D4', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(FadeIn(pattern))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(ORANGE))
        zoom_circle = Circle(radius=0.3, color=RED).move_to(self.grid['C3'])
        self.play(Create(zoom_circle))
        self.play(zoom_circle.animate.scale(0.5))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===

        final_text = Text("Chaotic Sensitivity", font_size=20, color=RED)
        self.place_at_grid(final_text, 'F3', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(final_text))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Conclusion and Intuition", [
            "Simple rules create infinite, beautiful complexity.",
            "Chaos thrives at the meeting of basins.",
            "Newton's method reveals structure within the unknown."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Simple rules create infinite, beautiful complexity.
        circle = Circle(radius=1.0, color=BLUE).set_stroke(width=4)

        dot = Dot(color=YELLOW)

        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"), run_time=1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===

        self.play(Create(line1), Create(line2))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"), run_time=1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Newton's method reveals structure within the unknown.
        final_text = Text("Newton's Wisdom", font_size=36, color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(final_text, 'F3')

outline.topic: From Tangents to Infinity: Newton's Method and Fractals

sections.title: Prerequisites: The Geometry of a Tangent
sections.content: Briefly introduce the tangent line as a linear approximation of a function at a point. Visual: A curve with a tangent line intersecting the x-axis.
sections.example: Imagine a drone calculating its landing spot: it estimates the ground slope at its current hover point to predict where it will touch down.

sections.title: Newton’s Method: The Iterative Search
sections.content: Explain the formula x_{n+1} = x_n - f(x_n)/f'(x_n). Focus on the 'Refinement' logic: each tangent intersection gets closer to the true root.
sections.example: A robotic arm finding the exact pressure point on a screen by repeatedly adjusting its position based on the slope of the glass resistance.

sections.title: The Basin of Attraction
sections.content: Explain that where you start (the 'initial guess') determines which root you find. Visual: A color-coded number line where different segments lead to different roots.
sections.example: Three hungry foxes standing at different points in a forest; each one runs to the closest watering hole (root), but some start too far and get confused.

sections.title: From Roots to Fractals: Newton's Fractal
sections.content: Extend the search to the Complex Plane. If we color each initial guess based on which root it converges to, complex patterns emerge at the boundaries.
sections.example: Visualizing the 'chaos' at the borders: zoom into a Newton Fractal for z^3 - 1 = 0, showing that even small changes in the starting position cause wild jumps between roots.

sections.title: Conclusion and Intuition
sections.content: Summarize how simple linear updates produce infinite complexity. Emphasize that chaos arises specifically where the 'basins' meet.
sections.example: A compass navigating a magnetic field: the complexity of the fractal boundary is like the unpredictable turbulence a ship faces when caught between two opposing currents.
